description: No user-facing English appears in French on the cover-letter editor, and none appears in any non-English locale on Job Search. A whole-namespace locale-parity test keeps translation files from drifting again.

userStories.title: The cover-letter editor is fully French in French
userStories.description: As a French user writing a cover letter, I want every label, hint and placeholder of the editor in French, including the sign-off options.
acceptanceCriteria: Locale files. `fr/common.json` has all 31 `coverLetters.editor.*` keys, translated, and the namespace-parity test passes for every namespace and locale.

No English on the page. On `/fr/dashboard/cover-letters/<id>/edit`, the recipient, opening, body, closing and signature sections show no English label, hint or placeholder (an e2e asserts the absence of the previous English fallbacks).
Sign-offs. The sign-off options come from keys in all four locales (for example fr "Cordialement,", "Bien à vous,"), and en is unchanged.
Stored values. A letter that already stores an English sign-off still displays it unchanged.

FR-1: One source per string: `jobs.json` for Job Search and `common.json` for the cover-letter editor. No hard-coded English remains on these surfaces except as an unreachable type-safety fallback, and the parity test makes any missing key fail.
FR-2: The parity test covers all namespaces and fails on any missing, extra or empty key.
FR-3: No dependency.

Regression constraint: Existing e2e for Job Search (`job-search-mobile`, `job-cv-template-picker`, `adaptation-modal-i18n`) and the cover-letter specs pass. Only assertions on the English text these stories replace may change, and en stays identical.
Regression constraint: Cover-letter save, generate and export flows are unchanged.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline.
Verification: The new namespace-parity unit test, which fails today on the 31 fr keys.
Verification: e2e text checks in fr and de for both surfaces.
Verification: `ui-expert` on both surfaces in fr and de, plus a text overflow check for longer translations. `code-reviewer`.
FAIL condition: Any listed English string visible in fr, de or it.
FAIL condition: Any en text change.
FAIL condition: The parity test does not fail when a key is removed from one locale (a control case is required).
BLOCKER condition: A string comes from the server or data rather than the UI. Report it; it stays out of scope.
Out of scope: Changing en wording.
Out of scope: Values that are legitimately identical across languages ("LinkedIn", "E-Mail"); there is no "must differ" rule.
Out of scope: API error messages (server text), canton names (codes shown as today), and other pages.
Out of scope: Merging en into other locales at runtime.

userStories.title: Job Search shows no English in fr, de or it
userStories.description: As a fr/de/it job seeker, I want Job Search's labels, toasts and dates in my language.
acceptanceCriteria: Keys. The 12 missing `jobs.json` keys and the new keys for the literals exist in all four locales. en values equal the current English text.

No English on the page. In fr, de and it on `/[locale]/dashboard/jobs`, none of the listed English strings is visible: "Live Data", "Notice", "All Cantons", "Loading…", "All N jobs loaded", "Preview", the full-details note, "View Full Job Details", "View in Applications", "Saving...", the save toasts, "Switzerland" and "Updated".
Dates. Dates on the job card and in the detail are formatted with the page locale (for example de "15.1.2026", fr "15/01/2026").
en unchanged. en text is unchanged.
